arguments.value: Judge Louise W. Flanagan was appointed to the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina by President George W. Bush in 2003, following service as a U.S. magistrate judge on the same court from 1995 to 2003. Born in Richmond, Virginia, she earned her B.A. from Wake Forest University and her J.D. from the University of Virginia School of Law. After clerking for Judge Malcolm J. Howard and practicing law in Washington, D.C., and Greenville, North Carolina, she built a distinguished judicial career, including serving as chief judge from 2004 to 2011.
